column1: # One row per envelope: the fixture's name, the exit status the run must end on,
# and what the case is there to hold. Exit 0 is a review (a `scope:` record), 1 a
# failure, 3 a reviewer that could not run. The runner checks the line as well as
# the number, so a case cannot pass by ending on the right status for a wrong reason.

column3: what it holds
a full report prints its coverage record
a working tree with no changes is an answer, not a failure
a run that read the range and found nothing is a review
a short verdict discussing quota handling is not a quota notice
a verdict may open by addressing the reader as "your usage"
and as "your organization"
Your usage of `jq -e` … is a finding, not an allowance
advising a larger model is advice, not a limit notice
API error handling is correct opens a verdict, not an error
so does "Your seat type validation is correct"
and "Your usage allocation handling reads the right field"
and a verdict about the group-limit branch
a finding may quote the notice fragments this script matches
including inside quotation marks rather than backticks
and may quote the machine suffix as well
a report written before the run broke is kept, under a warning
a turn sent to the background costs the report nothing
nor does it cost a short one its coverage record
an error inside the local command is not a review
nor is a refused login
nor is a missing one
a multi-line auth failure has a report's shape and no model behind it
neither has a crash's accumulated stack
an envelope with no `.result` still quotes what it does carry
a run cut off before writing anything names what cut it
a run that produced nothing quotes the envelope
a result of blanks is not a review with an empty body
an envelope with no fields answers nothing
a wording nobody anticipated is quoted, not classified
a filled context asks for a narrower range
a throttled request asks to be run again
even when it denies being a limit in words containing "usage limit"
and when the envelope carries no status at all
an unavailable API asks to be run again
with the envelope quoted where the run said nothing
a verdict whose usage came back zeroed is quoted, never filed as a limit
a verdict quoting a limit phrase is quoted back, not filed as one
a session limit is a reviewer to wait for
so is one worded as required credits
and one the status alone identifies
a limit reached after the models were billed is still a limit
a notice that outgrew a report's length is still a notice
an account limit naming a rate window is not a throttle
a spent balance arrives as a 400, not a 429
a 429 the notice did not explain stays retryable
and so does plain throttling under the same status
an organization out of credits
an organization's credit cap
the CLI's short spelling of the same, mid-run
and before a single model call
an allocation an admin turned off
a seat type that does not include usage
a service disabled for the organization
a group allowance set to zero
a model limit reached mid-run
a notice opening with the model's own name
including the variant that tells the reader to switch
and the one that names the command instead
credits exhausted after the models were billed
credits a long context needs and does not have
